checks.name: Lossless pre-dispatch atomicity and the post-claim guard
checks.method: read `reserve` (339-372), `commit` (476-513), `cancel` (466-474), `release_claims` (441-456), and `retain`'s lossless branch (427-429); read `test_lossless_backpressure_pre_dispatch` (740), `test_validity_effect_on_lossless_backpressure` (823), and preserved `test_lossless_reservations`; ran an independent read-only state-space model over capacities 1..16 (reserve/commit/cancel/retain) in `/tmp`
checks.result: pass: `reserve` increments `backpressure_rejections` and raises validity with `required_loss = true` for a matching full lossless tap, then returns `observation_backpressure` with no reservation and no other matching tap claimed, i.e. the provider is not mutated and no record is emitted. The post-claim `retain` branch (427-429) is a defensive guard: the model confirms `size + reserved_lossless <= record_capacity` is invariant, so a claimed lossless slot always reaches `retain` with `size <= record_capacity - 1 < record_capacity` and always appends; the branch is unreachable for capacities 1..16 and no test claims to exercise it. This matches the repaired NEG-05 classification.

checks.name: Applied declared validity effect and realized vocabulary
checks.result: pass: the raise target is selected solely by the declared effect (`none` -> `valid`, `degrade_on_loss` -> `degraded`, `invalidate_on_loss` -> `invalid`); `required_loss` forces at least `degraded`; the update is monotonic by encoded numeric value and is never raised without a matching loss. `to_string` returns exactly `"valid"`/`"degraded"`/`"invalid"`, and the enumerators encode `valid < degraded < invalid`. The three declarations are asserted for drop, coalesce-replacement, and lossless backpressure, including the accepted lossless `none` case that still degrades.
